key_insight: A fully local multi-agent AI system can deidentify multimodal hospital data with near-complete accuracy while preserving clinically important content.
clinical_relevance: This could enable safer secondary use of sensitive medical data for AI development, research, and sharing without relying on cloud-based tools.
method: Built a modular local framework combining multimodal LLMs, task-specific neural networks, and rule-based transformations.
Tested 16 orchestrator configurations on a benchmark spanning synthetic and real hospital data across text, CT, face images, handwriting, and audio.
Compared performance against leading proprietary and open-source solutions using deidentification and preservation metrics.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark including 250 MIMIC-IV patients plus local multimodal data, the best local configuration reached 98.80% per-patient deidentification sensitivity and 99.60% critical clinical preservation.
watch_item: Performance was benchmark-based, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation for rare edge cases, workflow integration, and privacy governance.
paper_title: The Multimodal Anonymizer: a fully local multi-agent AI system for medical data deidentification
